title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: ACL Person
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management (each non-executive director, Managing Director and Group CEO, CFO, Company Secretary) plus additional persons designated by the Board and listed in Appendix A (State CEOs, COO, CMO, CIO, GM SunDoctors, GM Commercial, Head of Investor Relations, Medical Director, CEO direct reports, Legal Counsel, Finance team members, EAs to a Director or State CEO), plus any company or trust controlled by such a person.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: seeks consent from the chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Other directors, Company Secretary and the Chief Financial Officer
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: seeks consent from the chair of the Board or, in their absence, the chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Any other ACL Person
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: seeks consent from the Company Secretary or, in their absence, the Chief Executive Officer.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: For the purposes of section 4 (Blackout Periods/notifications) only, ACL Person also includes a spouse (including de facto), child, close relative, or a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with a Director/Senior Management person.

definitions.hedging_definition: Operate to limit the economic risk of any ACL Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including ACL's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under any ACL incentive plan) on that ACL Person's behalf

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other Blackout Period from time to time; the policy does not state whether such additional periods are kept confidential.

rules.detail: Options and other derivative instruments over ACL securities are 'securities' for Blackout Period and consent purposes. Dealing is prohibited during a Blackout Period (absent a 4.3 exceptional-circumstances approval) and otherwise requires prior consent under 4.2; short-term or speculative derivative dealing is banned outright regardless of timing.
rules.evidence: prohibits the trading in shares, options, debentures (including convertible notes) and other securities

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt, the ACL Person seeking authorisation cannot be their own Authorising Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank must identify the correct independent Authorising Officer for the specific director/executive entering the collar; the Chair of the Board, for instance, cannot approve their own collar and must go to the Audit Committee chair.

bespoke_clauses.clause: prior to dealing in ACL securities outside a Blackout Period the person must notify the relevant person in paragraph 4.2(c) (the Authorising Officer) and the Company Secretary, by email, of their proposed dealing and obtain consent to trade from the Authorising Officer
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both the Authorising Officer and the Company Secretary must be notified before the collar is entered into, adding an extra notification step compared to policies with a single approver.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of ACL securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Gives the bank confidence that if it enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that disposal is an exempted dealing under the policy (only after-the-fact notice to the Authorising Officer is required), not a breach or a dealing needing fresh consent.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar is not possible over unvested ACL shares or vested shares still subject to a holding lock: section 5.2 bans all 'protection arrangements' (hedging, short selling beyond holding, anything limiting economic risk or profiting from a price fall) and section 5.3 bans granting any security or margin lending over such shares, with no consent pathway. Once the shares are vested and free of any holding lock, the same collar and loan-security package is permitted, but dealing must occur outside a Blackout Period (or under a 4.3 exceptional-circumstances approval) and requires prior consent from an independent Authorising Officer under 4.2 (who cannot be the ACL Person themselves), notification to the Company Secretary, a confirmation of no Inside Information, and a post-trade confirmation. The approver differs by seniority (Audit Committee chair, Board chair, or Company Secretary/CEO) but all ACL Persons follow the same substantive rules. If the bank later needs to enforce its security and sell the shares, that sale is an exempted dealing requiring only after-the-fact notice, not fresh clearance. No minimum shareholding requirement is referenced.
